title: Adaptive Kernel Blend Learner for Customer-Profiled Inference
creator: Marisol Reyes
description: Problem: The global kernel selection policy optimizes for aggregate workloads and often misallocates fast/cheap kernels for smaller high-SLA tenants or long-seq workloads. Mixed tenant traffic (short chat vs. long generation) and heterogeneous hardware (A100, H100, T4-like) produce suboptimal unit economics and tail latency. This ticket introduces a per-customer kernel profile and an online 'blend learner' that mixes kernels probabilistically according to learned rewards, bounded by a probe budget so production SLOs aren't violated.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant kernel profiles are recorded in the profile store (arch, seqlen histogram, kv-hit, prefilling ratio)
Runtime can compute a 3-kernel blend for a tenant given current features and use it for routing decisions
Probe budget enforcement prevents added tail-latency above SLA by more than 2ms p95 in controlled experiments
End-to-end canary: 5% traffic with learner enabled shows >=8% token-cost reduction for tenant subsets with stable seqlen distributions
Unit and integration tests for the profile store, learner, and probe scheduler merged and passing
technical_notes: Features to persist: gpu_arch, model_size, mean/median/p90 seqlen, prefill_ratio, kv_cache_hit_rate, recent-prefill-decode-ratio, temperature/use-case tag
Reward signal: composite score combining p50 latency penalty, p95 latency tail safety penalty, and token-cost delta vs baseline
Learner model: lightweight Bayesian bandit (Thompson sampling with beta priors) per-tenant for discrete kernel arms; fallback to global policy when tenant history < N samples
Probe mechanics: low-rate shadow requests + scheduled microbench per kernel variant; probe budget configurable per-tenant (tokens/hour or requests/hour)
Data pipeline: telemetry -> profile-aggregator -> profile-store (compact TTLed entries) -> online-learner service
Safety: deterministic fallback path, store-based kill-switch, and quota-enforced probe limiter. All probe decisions logged for audit and debugging.
proposed_solution: 1) Profile store schema (k,v flat): key=tenant_id, value=flat attributes (arch, seqlen_histogram_bucketed, kv_hit_pct, last_probe_ts)
2) Implement online blend learner as a service that exposes /recommend?tenant_id&context and returns a weighted kernel distribution (3 arms max)
3) Probe scheduler: token-budgeted, tenant-scoped; probes run as low-priority background calls with isolated resources and no customer-visible traffic unless validated

4) Runtime integration: adapter layer accepts weighted distribution and samples kernel per-request; implement sticky sampling so short-prefill/long-decode flows prefer consistent kernels within a session
5) Canary plan: start with internal tenants then incremental rollout to 1%, 5%, 25% with telemetry checks and automated rollback triggers
6) Observability: dashboard for per-tenant profile, probe counts, reward curves, and rollback triggers; add tracing for kernel decision path

risks_mitigation: Risk: Probing could increase tail latency if probes interfere with production queues. Mitigation: probes run at low priority on separate instance pools and respect GPU QoS limits
Risk: Tenant profiles may be stale and cause wrong choices. Mitigation: TTL profiles at 24h and prefer global fallback when history < threshold
Risk: Cost savings for some tenants but regressions for others. Mitigation: A/B guardrails and automatic immediate rollback for any tenant with >5% p95 regression
Risk: Complexity adds operational burden. Mitigation: limit blend size to max 3 kernels, provide human-readable explainability logs for recommendations
notes: This ticket intentionally constrains exploration to tenant-scoped bandits and a probe budget to reduce blast radius. Follow-on work can explore hierarchical multi-tenant learners and per-model variants once we validate safety and ROI.
